knowledge_checks.title: Revision Recall: PCA limits
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes principal component analysis?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Principal components are orthogonal variance-ordered linear combinations, useful for dimension reduction rather than causal inference.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: PCA summarises correlated variation with fewer orthogonal components and does not establish causation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating PCA as a causal or supervised modelling method.

choices.label: PCA forms orthogonal linear combinations of variables, ordered by explained sample variance. It can reduce dimension but does not by itself establish causal relationships.
PCA identifies which observed variables causally determine a response.
PCA retains every original variable unchanged while reducing dimension.
PCA maximises the variance of each original variable separately.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: discrete match
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A manufacturer independently inspects 40 items, each having the same probability p of being defective. What is the distribution of the number of defective items?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with constant success probability produces a binomial count.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Choosing hypergeometric without finite-population sampling without replacement.

choices.label: Hypergeometric, because the number of inspections is fixed.
Poisson with parameter p, regardless of the number inspected.
Geometric with parameter p, because each item is defective or not defective.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: continuous placement
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claims arrive according to a Poisson process with constant rate lambda. What is the distribution of the waiting time until the next claim?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Poisson-process interarrival times are exponentially distributed with constant hazard lambda.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: The waiting time is Exponential(lambda), with mean 1/lambda.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Confusing the Poisson count with the exponential interarrival time.

choices.label: Normal with mean 1/lambda because waiting times are continuous.
Poisson with mean lambda because the arrivals form a Poisson process.
Uniform on the next unit interval because the hazard is constant.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: Alpha association hinge
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two continuous variables have outliers and a strong monotone but nonlinear relationship. Which conclusion is justified?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Rank measures capture monotone association, while causation requires additional design or evidence.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use Spearman's rho or Kendall's tau and avoid a causal interpretation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assuming nonlinear association cannot be measured or that association proves causation.

choices.label: Spearman's rank correlation or Kendall's tau can measure the monotone association, but neither establishes causation.
Pearson correlation measures every monotone relationship exactly.
A significant rank correlation proves that one variable causes the other.
Correlation is necessarily zero whenever a relationship is nonlinear.

worked_example.title: Retrieve Binomial match for fixed independent trials
worked_example.problem_statement: Closed-book retrieval of one discrete-family hinge. A manufacturer independently inspects n = 25 items, each with the same probability p of being defective. Name the distribution of the number of defectives, and refuse one mismatched family that students often pick when n is fixed.

given.value: n = 25 independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Match the fixed independent-trial story to a named discrete family, then refuse a common mismatch.

steps.label: Match story to Binomial
steps.attempt_cue: Name the family for a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.
steps.explanation: A fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with constant success probability produces a binomial count.

steps.label: Refuse hypergeometric mismatch
steps.attempt_cue: Why is hypergeometric the wrong first match here?
steps.explanation: Hypergeometric requires sampling without replacement from a finite success/failure population. Independent inspections with constant p do not supply that story.
steps.calculation: Refuse hypergeometric without without-replacement finite draw story

steps.label: Refuse Normal count default
steps.attempt_cue: State why Normal is not the first match for this count.
steps.explanation: Normal has continuous all-real support and is a poor first match for a non-negative integer count of defectives.
steps.calculation: Refuse Normal-by-default for a discrete defective count

worked_example.final_answer: The number of defectives is Binomial(25, p). Refuse hypergeometric (no without-replacement finite-population story) and Normal-by-default for this count.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Choosing hypergeometric merely because the number of inspections is fixed, or defaulting to Normal because the response is a 'measurement'.
